He is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on continuous amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 6/17/2026-1/6/2027) plus metoprolol and warfarin. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 71/min with frequent atrial ectopy, QT 576 ms at RR ~1000 ms and a Bazett QTc of 576 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required, and a current ECG should be obtained as the only tracing on file is now more than four years old.

interpretations.explanation: 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm, mean ventricular rate 72/min (RR 788-924 ms, mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR 165 ms. Narrow QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT 356 ms at RR 838 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the 11/21/2025 tracing the rhythm is unchanged (sinus, though the earlier study had two atrial couplets with post-ectopic pauses) and the QTc has fallen markedly from 535 ms to 393 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

5/23/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with a short-normal PR of 104 ms. QRS 86 ms, QS/rS in V1 without terminal R', no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +1 degree (normal). QT 317 ms at RR 615 ms, QTc 404 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

9/17/2024, the only ECG on file. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging 410-728 ms and no organised or reproducible atrial activity (median-beat P amplitude only about 0.07 mV with poor beat-to-beat correlation), so there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 109/min. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in I, giving a frontal axis of about -59 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 321 ms at RR 550 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. This is consistent with the charted diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin. No prior tracing for comparison.

1/13/2019. Sinus bradycardia, dominant RR 1112-1160 ms (about 53/min) with one late couplet (RR 584/586 ms); nine QRS complexes give a mean rate of 59/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 162 ms. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -11 degrees (normal). QT 392 ms at RR 1130 ms, QTc 369 ms. Compared with 12/13/2018 (sinus 66/min, PR 176 ms, QRS 104 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change; the new finding is the atrial/ventricular couplet.

4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm with frequent atrial ectopy: the dominant RR intervals are 970-1086 ms (sinus rate about 58/min) with four early beats (426-674 ms); 12 complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 71/min. Low-amplitude but reproducible P waves (0.08-0.10 mV) are seen before the sinus beats on individual-beat review, with PR about 200 ms (borderline). QRS is narrow at 84 ms; frontal axis +43 degrees (normal). The T wave is very broad: QT 576 ms at RR about 1000 ms, Bazett QTc 576 ms - marked prolongation on amiodarone. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at 129/min with no P waves and QTc 449 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-900 ms) with upright P waves and PR 128 ms. QRS 98 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +33 degrees (normal). The T wave is late and broad: QT 504 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - significantly prolonged, relevant to his escitalopram therapy (the contemporaneous note called the QT 'acceptable'). Compared with 11/23/2022 (sinus 76/min, PR 120 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 367 ms) the QTc has increased by about 170 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

8/23/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, metronomically regular (RR 716-726 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 140 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms with rS in V1 and a tall R in V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 345 ms at RR 720 ms, QTc 407 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

7/13/2022. Sinus tachycardia at 141/min: RR intervals are regular at 404-454 ms and a reproducible P wave (peak about 0.09 mV in II/aVF, PR 120 ms) precedes each QRS. QRS 90 ms with a deep QS complex in V1; no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -9 degrees (normal). QT 278 ms at RR 426 ms, Bazett QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, chaotically irregular, no P waves) at 107/min with QTc 439 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

3/19/2025. Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular (RR 580-596 ms), tall upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 150 ms. QRS 92 ms; V1 shows an rSR' configuration with a small terminal S in I and V6, an incomplete right bundle branch block pattern that does not meet the 120 ms duration criterion, so no bundle branch block is reported. Frontal axis +45 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 437 ms. Identical to the 3/18/2025 tracing (102/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 437 ms); no change.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are chaotically irregular from 346 to 720 ms, there is no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval, and mean ventricular rate is 136/min. QRS 98 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -2 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms at RR 416 ms, Bazett QTc 453 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (17:13) showed the same rhythm at 134/min with QTc 433 ms, so there is no change between studies. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, extremely regular (RR 494-502 ms). An upright P wave with PR about 190 ms precedes each QRS, followed by PR-segment depression. QRS 102 ms without a bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis +51 degrees (normal). QT 286 ms at RR 498 ms, QTc 405 ms. Compared with the 9/16/2016 tracing (sinus 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 403 ms) there is no significant change.

7/16/2022. Regular sinus rhythm at 91/min (RR 650-666 ms). Discrete upright P waves in II and aVF with PR 185 ms - within normal limits. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -44 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 342 ms at RR 658 ms, QTc 421 ms. Compared with the prior 5/16/2021 tracing the rhythm remains sinus, QRS duration is unchanged and QTc is similar (399 to 421 ms, <60 ms change); the axis has shifted leftward but no listed change category applies.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm, dominant RR 864-882 ms with one early beat; mean rate 72/min. The atrial deflection preceding each QRS is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (P axis roughly -80 degrees), which is not sinus - this is an ectopic low-atrial/left-atrial rhythm, hence classified as OTHER. PR 130 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; net frontal QRS axis about -26 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 413 ms at RR 875 ms, Bazett QTc 442 ms. The prior 4/27/2025 tracing showed the same inverted inferior P waves at 61/min with QTc 412 ms and a markedly different, extreme frontal axis (-174 degrees) suggesting limb-lead reversal on that study; no listed change category applies.

4/29/2026, the only ECG on file. Regular rhythm at 70/min (RR 842-884 ms) with a small consistent atrial deflection before each QRS and PR 134 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block. As recorded, the QRS is deeply negative in I and aVL and positive in III with a positive R in V6, giving a frontal axis of about -172 degrees, which falls in the extreme axis range; the discordance between the limb leads and the normal precordial progression, together with an inverted P wave in lead I, strongly suggests left-arm/right-arm electrode reversal, and this should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. QT 362 ms at RR 862 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal, which is reassuring given his escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104/min (mild sinus tachycardia), RR 570-586 ms and regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 170 ms. QRS 104 ms with rS in V1 and no terminal R', so no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +24 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 578 ms, QTc 442 ms. The prior 6/20/2025 tracing was also sinus, then at 147/min with QRS 84 ms and QTc 406 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc difference is under 60 ms, so no listed change.

11/24/2025. Underlying sinus rhythm with dominant RR 944-980 ms (sinus rate about 62/min) interrupted by three early beats (RR 474-508 ms); 12 QRS complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 72/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 180 ms. QRS 104 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT 551 ms at RR 965 ms, Bazett QTc 561 ms - significantly prolonged on amiodarone. Compared with the 6/7/2025 tracing (sinus bradycardia, QTc 417 ms) the QTc has risen by about 144 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and QRS are otherwise unchanged.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112/min. RR intervals cluster tightly at 502/538/572 ms with a repeating pattern rather than the random irregularity of fibrillation, and a consistent upright P wave (about 0.10 mV in II and aVF) precedes every QRS with PR 185 ms, so this is sinus rather than the atrial flutter recorded in the problem list. QRS 102 ms with a deep S in V1 and a small terminal r, not meeting criteria for bundle branch block. Frontal axis +31 degrees (normal). QT 295 ms at RR 538 ms, QTc 402 ms. Essentially unchanged from the 7/4/2022 tracing (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR 167 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 396 ms).

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, very regular (RR 1144-1178 ms). Broad but upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 185 ms - no AV block. QRS 94 ms with rS in V1 and a tall R in V6; no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 436 ms at RR 1160 ms, QTc 404 ms. The prior 5/22/2023 tracing was also sinus bradycardia (58/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 396 ms) with one premature beat; no interval or rhythm change of note.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular (RR 1074-1116 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF but PR is prolonged at about 225 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis +5 degrees (normal). QT 408 ms at RR 1110 ms, QTc 388 ms. The prior 11/30/2024 tracing showed sinus rhythm in ventricular bigeminy (coupling interval 310 ms) with PR about 180-225 ms and QTc 434 ms; rhythm remains sinus, no new bundle branch block, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

4/19/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 492-500 ms and regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +64 degrees (normal). QT 292 ms at RR 496 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. No prior tracing is available for comparison, so no changes can be assessed.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 102/min (borderline sinus tachycardia), regular with prominent upright P waves and PR 142 ms. QRS 96 ms with a deep S in V1 and tall R in V6, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +50 degrees (normal). QT 324 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 422 ms. This is a repeat of the tracing recorded 34 seconds earlier (100/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is unchanged from it.

4/27/2022. 8/23/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, metronomically regular (RR 716-726 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 140 ms. 7/13/2022. Sinus tachycardia at 141/min: RR intervals are regular at 404-454 ms and a reproducible P wave (peak about 0.09 mV in II/aVF, PR 120 ms) precedes each QRS. Frontal axis +45 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 437 ms. Identical to the 3/18/2025 tracing (102/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 437 ms); no change.

4/19/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 492-500 ms and regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block. 8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 102/min (borderline sinus tachycardia), regular with prominent upright P waves and PR 142 ms. QRS 96 ms with a deep S in V1 and tall R in V6, no bundle branch block. arguments.explanation: 3/8/2026, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 856-906 ms), with tall upright P waves in II/aVF and PR 140 ms. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 8/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 8/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 9/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. This 95-year-old patient is also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1); secondary stroke prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended. History of falling and thrombocytopenia are noted and should be weighed at review.

interpretations.explanation: 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm, mean ventricular rate 72/min (RR 788-924 ms, mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR 165 ms. Narrow QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT 356 ms at RR 838 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the 11/21/2025 tracing the rhythm is unchanged (sinus, though the earlier study had two atrial couplets with post-ectopic pauses) and the QTc has fallen markedly from 535 ms to 393 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

5/23/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with a short-normal PR of 104 ms. QRS 86 ms, QS/rS in V1 without terminal R', no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +1 degree (normal). QT 317 ms at RR 615 ms, QTc 404 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

9/17/2024, the only ECG on file. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging 410-728 ms and no organised or reproducible atrial activity (median-beat P amplitude only about 0.07 mV with poor beat-to-beat correlation), so there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 109/min. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in I, giving a frontal axis of about -59 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 321 ms at RR 550 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. This is consistent with the charted diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin. No prior tracing for comparison.

1/13/2019. Sinus bradycardia, dominant RR 1112-1160 ms (about 53/min) with one late couplet (RR 584/586 ms); nine QRS complexes give a mean rate of 59/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 162 ms. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -11 degrees (normal). QT 392 ms at RR 1130 ms, QTc 369 ms. Compared with 12/13/2018 (sinus 66/min, PR 176 ms, QRS 104 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change; the new finding is the atrial/ventricular couplet.

4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm with frequent atrial ectopy: the dominant RR intervals are 970-1086 ms (sinus rate about 58/min) with four early beats (426-674 ms); 12 complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 71/min. Low-amplitude but reproducible P waves (0.08-0.10 mV) are seen before the sinus beats on individual-beat review, with PR about 200 ms (borderline). QRS is narrow at 84 ms; frontal axis +43 degrees (normal). The T wave is very broad: QT 576 ms at RR about 1000 ms, Bazett QTc 576 ms - marked prolongation on amiodarone. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at 129/min with no P waves and QTc 449 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-900 ms) with upright P waves and PR 128 ms. QRS 98 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +33 degrees (normal). The T wave is late and broad: QT 504 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - significantly prolonged, relevant to his escitalopram therapy (the contemporaneous note called the QT 'acceptable'). Compared with 11/23/2022 (sinus 76/min, PR 120 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 367 ms) the QTc has increased by about 170 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

8/23/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, metronomically regular (RR 716-726 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 140 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, chaotically irregular, no P waves) at 107/min with QTc 439 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

The prior 4/27/2025 tracing showed the same inverted inferior P waves at 61/min with QTc 412 ms and a markedly different, extreme frontal axis (-174 degrees) suggesting limb-lead reversal on that study; no listed change category applies.

QT 362 ms at RR 862 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal, which is reassuring given his escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 7/12/2026-1/9/2027, started 11/10/2025). His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 72/min with QT 551 ms and RR 965 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of 561 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 6/9/2026), so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. He is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on continuous amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 6/17/2026-1/6/2027) plus metoprolol and warfarin. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 71/min with frequent atrial ectopy, QT 576 ms at RR ~1000 ms and a Bazett QTc of 576 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required, and a current ECG should be obtained as the only tracing on file is now more than four years old.

interpretations.explanation: 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm, mean ventricular rate 72/min (RR 788-924 ms, mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR 165 ms. Narrow QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT 356 ms at RR 838 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the 11/21/2025 tracing the rhythm is unchanged (sinus, though the earlier study had two atrial couplets with post-ectopic pauses) and the QTc has fallen markedly from 535 ms to 393 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

5/23/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with a short-normal PR of 104 ms. QRS 86 ms, QS/rS in V1 without terminal R', no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +1 degree (normal). QT 317 ms at RR 615 ms, QTc 404 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

9/17/2024, the only ECG on file. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging 410-728 ms and no organised or reproducible atrial activity (median-beat P amplitude only about 0.07 mV with poor beat-to-beat correlation), so there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 109/min. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in I, giving a frontal axis of about -59 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 321 ms at RR 550 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. This is consistent with the charted diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin. No prior tracing for comparison.

1/13/2019. Sinus bradycardia, dominant RR 1112-1160 ms (about 53/min) with one late couplet (RR 584/586 ms); nine QRS complexes give a mean rate of 59/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 162 ms. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -11 degrees (normal). QT 392 ms at RR 1130 ms, QTc 369 ms. Compared with 12/13/2018 (sinus 66/min, PR 176 ms, QRS 104 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change; the new finding is the atrial/ventricular couplet.

4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm with frequent atrial ectopy: the dominant RR intervals are 970-1086 ms (sinus rate about 58/min) with four early beats (426-674 ms); 12 complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 71/min. Low-amplitude but reproducible P waves (0.08-0.10 mV) are seen before the sinus beats on individual-beat review, with PR about 200 ms (borderline). QRS is narrow at 84 ms; frontal axis +43 degrees (normal). The T wave is very broad: QT 576 ms at RR about 1000 ms, Bazett QTc 576 ms - marked prolongation on amiodarone. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at 129/min with no P waves and QTc 449 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-900 ms) with upright P waves and PR 128 ms. QRS 98 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +33 degrees (normal). The T wave is late and broad: QT 504 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - significantly prolonged, relevant to his escitalopram therapy (the contemporaneous note called the QT 'acceptable'). Compared with 11/23/2022 (sinus 76/min, PR 120 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 367 ms) the QTc has increased by about 170 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

8/23/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, metronomically regular (RR 716-726 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 140 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms with rS in V1 and a tall R in V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 345 ms at RR 720 ms, QTc 407 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

7/13/2022. Sinus tachycardia at 141/min: RR intervals are regular at 404-454 ms and a reproducible P wave (peak about 0.09 mV in II/aVF, PR 120 ms) precedes each QRS. QRS 90 ms with a deep QS complex in V1; no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -9 degrees (normal). QT 278 ms at RR 426 ms, Bazett QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, chaotically irregular, no P waves) at 107/min with QTc 439 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

3/19/2025. Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular (RR 580-596 ms), tall upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 150 ms. QRS 92 ms; V1 shows an rSR' configuration with a small terminal S in I and V6, an incomplete right bundle branch block pattern that does not meet the 120 ms duration criterion, so no bundle branch block is reported. Frontal axis +45 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 437 ms. Identical to the 3/18/2025 tracing (102/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 437 ms); no change.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are chaotically irregular from 346 to 720 ms, there is no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval, and mean ventricular rate is 136/min. QRS 98 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -2 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms at RR 416 ms, Bazett QTc 453 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (17:13) showed the same rhythm at 134/min with QTc 433 ms, so there is no change between studies. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, extremely regular (RR 494-502 ms). An upright P wave with PR about 190 ms precedes each QRS, followed by PR-segment depression. QRS 102 ms without a bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis +51 degrees (normal). QT 286 ms at RR 498 ms, QTc 405 ms. Compared with the 9/16/2016 tracing (sinus 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 403 ms) there is no significant change.

7/16/2022. Regular sinus rhythm at 91/min (RR 650-666 ms). Discrete upright P waves in II and aVF with PR 185 ms - within normal limits. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -44 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 342 ms at RR 658 ms, QTc 421 ms. Compared with the prior 5/16/2021 tracing the rhythm remains sinus, QRS duration is unchanged and QTc is similar (399 to 421 ms, <60 ms change); the axis has shifted leftward but no listed change category applies.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm, dominant RR 864-882 ms with one early beat; mean rate 72/min. The atrial deflection preceding each QRS is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (P axis roughly -80 degrees), which is not sinus - this is an ectopic low-atrial/left-atrial rhythm, hence classified as OTHER. PR 130 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; net frontal QRS axis about -26 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 413 ms at RR 875 ms, Bazett QTc 442 ms. The prior 4/27/2025 tracing showed the same inverted inferior P waves at 61/min with QTc 412 ms and a markedly different, extreme frontal axis (-174 degrees) suggesting limb-lead reversal on that study; no listed change category applies.

4/29/2026, the only ECG on file. Regular rhythm at 70/min (RR 842-884 ms) with a small consistent atrial deflection before each QRS and PR 134 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block. As recorded, the QRS is deeply negative in I and aVL and positive in III with a positive R in V6, giving a frontal axis of about -172 degrees, which falls in the extreme axis range; the discordance between the limb leads and the normal precordial progression, together with an inverted P wave in lead I, strongly suggests left-arm/right-arm electrode reversal, and this should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. QT 362 ms at RR 862 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal, which is reassuring given his escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation: RR intervals are grossly irregular (458-1150 ms), no discrete P waves are present (median-beat atrial amplitude about 0.02 mV, poor beat-to-beat correlation) and there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 70/min. QRS 96 ms with rS in V1, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +26 degrees (normal). QT 445 ms at RR 740 ms, Bazett QTc 517 ms - prolonged, in the context of amiodarone loading during this admission. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves (PR 170 ms) and QTc 403 ms, so this shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of more than 60 ms.

3/8/2026, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 856-906 ms), with tall upright P waves in II/aVF and PR 140 ms. QRS 96 ms, predominantly negative in V1 without a terminal R', so no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +54 degrees (normal). QT 430 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 458 ms - upper normal/borderline but below the 500 ms review threshold, which is relevant as this tracing was obtained to screen his newly started escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

2/15/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 76/min with only minor RR variation (mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 185 ms - within normal limits. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis +55 degrees (normal). QT 384 ms at RR 810 ms, Bazett QTc 426 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104/min (mild sinus tachycardia), RR 570-586 ms and regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 170 ms. QRS 104 ms with rS in V1 and no terminal R', so no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +24 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 578 ms, QTc 442 ms. The prior 6/20/2025 tracing was also sinus, then at 147/min with QRS 84 ms and QTc 406 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc difference is under 60 ms, so no listed change.

11/24/2025. Underlying sinus rhythm with dominant RR 944-980 ms (sinus rate about 62/min) interrupted by three early beats (RR 474-508 ms); 12 QRS complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 72/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 180 ms. QRS 104 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT 551 ms at RR 965 ms, Bazett QTc 561 ms - significantly prolonged on amiodarone. Compared with the 6/7/2025 tracing (sinus bradycardia, QTc 417 ms) the QTc has risen by about 144 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and QRS are otherwise unchanged.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112/min. RR intervals cluster tightly at 502/538/572 ms with a repeating pattern rather than the random irregularity of fibrillation, and a consistent upright P wave (about 0.10 mV in II and aVF) precedes every QRS with PR 185 ms, so this is sinus rather than the atrial flutter recorded in the problem list. QRS 102 ms with a deep S in V1 and a small terminal r, not meeting criteria for bundle branch block. Frontal axis +31 degrees (normal). QT 295 ms at RR 538 ms, QTc 402 ms. Essentially unchanged from the 7/4/2022 tracing (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR 167 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 396 ms).

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, very regular (RR 1144-1178 ms). Broad but upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 185 ms - no AV block. QRS 94 ms with rS in V1 and a tall R in V6; no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 436 ms at RR 1160 ms, QTc 404 ms. The prior 5/22/2023 tracing was also sinus bradycardia (58/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 396 ms) with one premature beat; no interval or rhythm change of note.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular (RR 1074-1116 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF but PR is prolonged at about 225 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis +5 degrees (normal). QT 408 ms at RR 1110 ms, QTc 388 ms. The prior 11/30/2024 tracing showed sinus rhythm in ventricular bigeminy (coupling interval 310 ms) with PR about 180-225 ms and QTc 434 ms; rhythm remains sinus, no new bundle branch block, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

4/19/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 492-500 ms and regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +64 degrees (normal). QT 292 ms at RR 496 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. No prior tracing is available for comparison, so no changes can be assessed.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 102/min (borderline sinus tachycardia), regular with prominent upright P waves and PR 142 ms. QRS 96 ms with a deep S in V1 and tall R in V6, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +50 degrees (normal). QT 324 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 422 ms. This is a repeat of the tracing recorded 34 seconds earlier (100/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is unchanged from it.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 9/12/2025 and most recently 6/22/2026). She has had no anticoagulant since the apixaban course ended in February 2025; current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only, so she is on antiplatelet therapy alone. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (Class 1) is absent; aspirin is not an acceptable substitute. Needs prescriber review to start a DOAC unless a documented contraindication exists.

Patient has taken escitalopram 10 mg daily since 5/14/2024 and the prescription is current (7/18/2026-12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min, QT 504 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - above the 500 ms review threshold. Of note the 5/14/2024 clinic note reviewed this same tracing and recorded 'sinus rhythm, QT acceptable', which understates the measured QTc. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027, continuously prescribed since at least 10/2023). Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 71/min with QT 516 ms at RR 845 ms, Bazett QTc 557 ms, above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. The dose also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised in patients with QT prolongation; prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 11/10/2025 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start was on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. A 12-lead ECG was recorded on 11/24/2025 (14 days), so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 561 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was first prescribed at the 2/12/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. A 12-lead ECG was obtained on 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start), showing sinus rhythm with QTc 458 ms; the requirement was met within the required time.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 3/2/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. A 12-lead ECG was obtained on 3/7/2026 (5 days), sinus rhythm with QTc 383 ms, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was first prescribed at the 4/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window (it would have satisfied the superseded 30-day rule but not the 14-day rule). No qualifying ECG was obtained by the due date, which has passed, so the requirement is overdue; the 4/29/2026 tracing (sinus rhythm, QTc 390 ms) can be used to document late completion.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 8/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been recorded since. The due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 8/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing or report is in the chart. That outside ECG could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 9/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since the start (the most recent tracing is 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the clinician documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, with a plan to recheck. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a clinician-made dose change, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was met.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (chart diagnosis, carried in all cardiology notes through 6/27/2026) and no anticoagulant at any time in the record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), for which oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the chart also lists 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure', so the risk/benefit discussion and bleeding history should be reviewed by the prescriber before starting.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the protocol after a home INR of 3.4 (a dose change a clinic pharmacist is authorised to make under the standing order). Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change and the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue. This 95-year-old patient is also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a documented prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia/ataxia. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in this chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1); secondary stroke prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended. History of falling and thrombocytopenia are noted and should be weighed at review.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in every cardiology clinic note (7/19/2025 through 8/4/2026). Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant, and the last warfarin/amiodarone exposure was during the February-March 2025 admission. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy 1, hypertension 1), which meets the threshold at which oral anticoagulation is recommended in men. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. No cardiology decision to resume is recorded, yet apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed on 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) and is still listed as a current medication in the 8/20/2026 clinic note, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. A current anticoagulant is therefore running despite a documented major bleed and an explicit instruction that it should not continue without review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026). However rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-prescribed the same day (order valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped; the 7/15/2026 medication list itself shows both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active as of the evaluation date in a patient who also takes clopidogrel and has CLL with prior anaemia/rectal haemorrhage - a high bleeding-risk overlap that needs immediate reconciliation.

arguments.explanation: 3/7/2026, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 81/min; RR intervals vary smoothly from 658 to 858 ms (sinus arrhythmia) and a large reproducible upright P wave (0.14 mV in II and aVF) precedes every QRS with PR 180 ms, followed by mild PR-segment depression. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 327 ms at RR 730 ms, Bazett QTc 383 ms - normal, reassuring on citalopram 40 mg daily. This tracing confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm and satisfies the post-start ECG requirement for citalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 9/12/2025 and most recently 6/22/2026). She has had no anticoagulant since the apixaban course ended in February 2025; current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only, so she is on antiplatelet therapy alone. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (Class 1) is absent; aspirin is not an acceptable substitute. Needs prescriber review to start a DOAC unless a documented contraindication exists.

Patient has taken escitalopram 10 mg daily since 5/14/2024 and the prescription is current (7/18/2026-12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min, QT 504 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - above the 500 ms review threshold. Of note the 5/14/2024 clinic note reviewed this same tracing and recorded 'sinus rhythm, QT acceptable', which understates the measured QTc. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027, continuously prescribed since at least 10/2023). Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 71/min with QT 516 ms at RR 845 ms, Bazett QTc 557 ms, above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. The dose also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised in patients with QT prolongation; prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 11/10/2025 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start was on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. A 12-lead ECG was recorded on 11/24/2025 (14 days), so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 561 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was first prescribed at the 2/12/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. A 12-lead ECG was obtained on 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start), showing sinus rhythm with QTc 458 ms; the requirement was met within the required time.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 3/2/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. A 12-lead ECG was obtained on 3/7/2026 (5 days), sinus rhythm with QTc 383 ms, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was first prescribed at the 4/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window (it would have satisfied the superseded 30-day rule but not the 14-day rule). No qualifying ECG was obtained by the due date, which has passed, so the requirement is overdue; the 4/29/2026 tracing (sinus rhythm, QTc 390 ms) can be used to document late completion.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 8/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been recorded since. The due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 8/10/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing or report is in the chart. That outside ECG could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the 9/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since the start (the most recent tracing is 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the clinician documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, with a plan to recheck. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a clinician-made dose change, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was met.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (chart diagnosis, carried in all cardiology notes through 6/27/2026) and no anticoagulant at any time in the record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), for which oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the chart also lists 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure', so the risk/benefit discussion and bleeding history should be reviewed by the prescriber before starting.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the protocol after a home INR of 3.4 (a dose change a clinic pharmacist is authorised to make under the standing order). Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change and the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue. This 95-year-old patient is also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a documented prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia/ataxia. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in this chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1); secondary stroke prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended. History of falling and thrombocytopenia are noted and should be weighed at review.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in every cardiology clinic note (7/19/2025 through 8/4/2026). Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant, and the last warfarin/amiodarone exposure was during the February-March 2025 admission. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy 1, hypertension 1), which meets the threshold at which oral anticoagulation is recommended in men. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. No cardiology decision to resume is recorded, yet apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed on 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) and is still listed as a current medication in the 8/20/2026 clinic note, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. A current anticoagulant is therefore running despite a documented major bleed and an explicit instruction that it should not continue without review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026). However rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-prescribed the same day (order valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped; the 7/15/2026 medication list itself shows both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active as of the evaluation date in a patient who also takes clopidogrel and has CLL with prior anaemia/rectal haemorrhage - a high bleeding-risk overlap that needs immediate reconciliation.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13:50 and 19:36:45) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves and RR intervals ranging 346-720 ms - atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of about 134-136/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the note should be corrected and rate control/anticoagulation reviewed.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 7/12/2026-1/9/2027, started 11/10/2025). His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 72/min with QT 551 ms and RR 965 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of 561 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 6/9/2026), so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. He is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on continuous amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 6/17/2026-1/6/2027) plus metoprolol and warfarin. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 71/min with frequent atrial ectopy, QT 576 ms at RR ~1000 ms and a Bazett QTc of 576 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required, and a current ECG should be obtained as the only tracing on file is now more than four years old.

interpretations.explanation: 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm, mean ventricular rate 72/min (RR 788-924 ms, mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR 165 ms. Narrow QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT 356 ms at RR 838 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the 11/21/2025 tracing the rhythm is unchanged (sinus, though the earlier study had two atrial couplets with post-ectopic pauses) and the QTc has fallen markedly from 535 ms to 393 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

5/23/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with a short-normal PR of 104 ms. QRS 86 ms, QS/rS in V1 without terminal R', no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +1 degree (normal). QT 317 ms at RR 615 ms, QTc 404 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

9/17/2024, the only ECG on file. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging 410-728 ms and no organised or reproducible atrial activity (median-beat P amplitude only about 0.07 mV with poor beat-to-beat correlation), so there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 109/min. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in I, giving a frontal axis of about -59 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 321 ms at RR 550 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. This is consistent with the charted diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin. No prior tracing for comparison.

1/13/2019. Sinus bradycardia, dominant RR 1112-1160 ms (about 53/min) with one late couplet (RR 584/586 ms); nine QRS complexes give a mean rate of 59/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 162 ms. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -11 degrees (normal). QT 392 ms at RR 1130 ms, QTc 369 ms. Compared with 12/13/2018 (sinus 66/min, PR 176 ms, QRS 104 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change; the new finding is the atrial/ventricular couplet.

4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm with frequent atrial ectopy: the dominant RR intervals are 970-1086 ms (sinus rate about 58/min) with four early beats (426-674 ms); 12 complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 71/min. Low-amplitude but reproducible P waves (0.08-0.10 mV) are seen before the sinus beats on individual-beat review, with PR about 200 ms (borderline). QRS is narrow at 84 ms; frontal axis +43 degrees (normal). The T wave is very broad: QT 576 ms at RR about 1000 ms, Bazett QTc 576 ms - marked prolongation on amiodarone. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at 129/min with no P waves and QTc 449 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-900 ms) with upright P waves and PR 128 ms. QRS 98 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +33 degrees (normal). The T wave is late and broad: QT 504 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - significantly prolonged, relevant to his escitalopram therapy (the contemporaneous note called the QT 'acceptable'). Compared with 11/23/2022 (sinus 76/min, PR 120 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 367 ms) the QTc has increased by about 170 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

8/23/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, metronomically regular (RR 716-726 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 140 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms with rS in V1 and a tall R in V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 345 ms at RR 720 ms, QTc 407 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

7/13/2022. Sinus tachycardia at 141/min: RR intervals are regular at 404-454 ms and a reproducible P wave (peak about 0.09 mV in II/aVF, PR 120 ms) precedes each QRS. QRS 90 ms with a deep QS complex in V1; no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -9 degrees (normal). QT 278 ms at RR 426 ms, Bazett QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, chaotically irregular, no P waves) at 107/min with QTc 439 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

3/19/2025. Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular (RR 580-596 ms), tall upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 150 ms. QRS 92 ms; V1 shows an rSR' configuration with a small terminal S in I and V6, an incomplete right bundle branch block pattern that does not meet the 120 ms duration criterion, so no bundle branch block is reported. Frontal axis +45 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 437 ms. Identical to the 3/18/2025 tracing (102/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 437 ms); no change.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are chaotically irregular from 346 to 720 ms, there is no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval, and mean ventricular rate is 136/min. QRS 98 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -2 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms at RR 416 ms, Bazett QTc 453 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (17:13) showed the same rhythm at 134/min with QTc 433 ms, so there is no change between studies. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, extremely regular (RR 494-502 ms). An upright P wave with PR about 190 ms precedes each QRS, followed by PR-segment depression. QRS 102 ms without a bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis +51 degrees (normal). QT 286 ms at RR 498 ms, QTc 405 ms. Compared with the 9/16/2016 tracing (sinus 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 403 ms) there is no significant change.

7/16/2022. Regular sinus rhythm at 91/min (RR 650-666 ms). Discrete upright P waves in II and aVF with PR 185 ms - within normal limits. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -44 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 342 ms at RR 658 ms, QTc 421 ms. Compared with the prior 5/16/2021 tracing the rhythm remains sinus, QRS duration is unchanged and QTc is similar (399 to 421 ms, <60 ms change); the axis has shifted leftward but no listed change category applies.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm, dominant RR 864-882 ms with one early beat; mean rate 72/min. The atrial deflection preceding each QRS is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (P axis roughly -80 degrees), which is not sinus - this is an ectopic low-atrial/left-atrial rhythm, hence classified as OTHER. PR 130 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; net frontal QRS axis about -26 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 413 ms at RR 875 ms, Bazett QTc 442 ms. The prior 4/27/2025 tracing showed the same inverted inferior P waves at 61/min with QTc 412 ms and a markedly different, extreme frontal axis (-174 degrees) suggesting limb-lead reversal on that study; no listed change category applies.

4/29/2026, the only ECG on file. Regular rhythm at 70/min (RR 842-884 ms) with a small consistent atrial deflection before each QRS and PR 134 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block. As recorded, the QRS is deeply negative in I and aVL and positive in III with a positive R in V6, giving a frontal axis of about -172 degrees, which falls in the extreme axis range; the discordance between the limb leads and the normal precordial progression, together with an inverted P wave in lead I, strongly suggests left-arm/right-arm electrode reversal, and this should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. QT 362 ms at RR 862 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal, which is reassuring given his escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation: RR intervals are grossly irregular (458-1150 ms), no discrete P waves are present (median-beat atrial amplitude about 0.02 mV, poor beat-to-beat correlation) and there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 70/min. QRS 96 ms with rS in V1, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +26 degrees (normal). QT 445 ms at RR 740 ms, Bazett QTc 517 ms - prolonged, in the context of amiodarone loading during this admission. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves (PR 170 ms) and QTc 403 ms, so this shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of more than 60 ms.

3/8/2026, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 856-906 ms), with tall upright P waves in II/aVF and PR 140 ms. QRS 96 ms, predominantly negative in V1 without a terminal R', so no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +54 degrees (normal). QT 430 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 458 ms - upper normal/borderline but below the 500 ms review threshold, which is relevant as this tracing was obtained to screen his newly started escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

2/15/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 76/min with only minor RR variation (mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 185 ms - within normal limits. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis +55 degrees (normal). QT 384 ms at RR 810 ms, Bazett QTc 426 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus rhythm at 122/min, metronomically regular (RR 492-496 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 128 ms. QRS has narrowed to 96 ms and no longer meets criteria for bundle branch block. The QRS is predominantly negative in I, aVL and V6 and positive in III, giving a frontal axis of about +177 degrees - right axis deviation. QT 290 ms at RR 494 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (01:33), which showed a wide 164 ms QRS with a monophasic late-peaking R in V1 and broad S waves in I and V6 (right bundle branch block) and QTc 478 ms, the bundle branch block has resolved and the QTc has fallen by about 65 ms.

9/13/2025. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (312-604 ms), the baseline shows no organised atrial activity and there is no measurable PR interval; mean ventricular rate 147/min. QRS 104 ms without a bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis -24 degrees (normal). QT 272 ms at RR 396 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 84/min with discrete P waves (PR 140 ms) and frequent ectopy, QTc 425 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation; the QTc is unchanged.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104/min (mild sinus tachycardia), RR 570-586 ms and regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 170 ms. QRS 104 ms with rS in V1 and no terminal R', so no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +24 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 578 ms, QTc 442 ms. The prior 6/20/2025 tracing was also sinus, then at 147/min with QRS 84 ms and QTc 406 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc difference is under 60 ms, so no listed change.

11/24/2025. Underlying sinus rhythm with dominant RR 944-980 ms (sinus rate about 62/min) interrupted by three early beats (RR 474-508 ms); 12 QRS complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 72/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 180 ms. QRS 104 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT 551 ms at RR 965 ms, Bazett QTc 561 ms - significantly prolonged on amiodarone. Compared with the 6/7/2025 tracing (sinus bradycardia, QTc 417 ms) the QTc has risen by about 144 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and QRS are otherwise unchanged.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112/min. RR intervals cluster tightly at 502/538/572 ms with a repeating pattern rather than the random irregularity of fibrillation, and a consistent upright P wave (about 0.10 mV in II and aVF) precedes every QRS with PR 185 ms, so this is sinus rather than the atrial flutter recorded in the problem list. QRS 102 ms with a deep S in V1 and a small terminal r, not meeting criteria for bundle branch block. Frontal axis +31 degrees (normal). QT 295 ms at RR 538 ms, QTc 402 ms. Essentially unchanged from the 7/4/2022 tracing (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR 167 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 396 ms).

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, very regular (RR 1144-1178 ms). Broad but upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 185 ms - no AV block. QRS 94 ms with rS in V1 and a tall R in V6; no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 436 ms at RR 1160 ms, QTc 404 ms. The prior 5/22/2023 tracing was also sinus bradycardia (58/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 396 ms) with one premature beat; no interval or rhythm change of note.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular (RR 1074-1116 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF but PR is prolonged at about 225 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis +5 degrees (normal). QT 408 ms at RR 1110 ms, QTc 388 ms. The prior 11/30/2024 tracing showed sinus rhythm in ventricular bigeminy (coupling interval 310 ms) with PR about 180-225 ms and QTc 434 ms; rhythm remains sinus, no new bundle branch block, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

4/19/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 492-500 ms and regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +64 degrees (normal). QT 292 ms at RR 496 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. No prior tracing is available for comparison, so no changes can be assessed.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 102/min (borderline sinus tachycardia), regular with prominent upright P waves and PR 142 ms. QRS 96 ms with a deep S in V1 and tall R in V6, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +50 degrees (normal). QT 324 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 422 ms. This is a repeat of the tracing recorded 34 seconds earlier (100/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is unchanged from it.

A current anticoagulant is therefore running despite a documented major bleed and an explicit instruction that it should not continue without review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026). However rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-prescribed the same day (order valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped; the 7/15/2026 medication list itself shows both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active as of the evaluation date in a patient who also takes clopidogrel and has CLL with prior anaemia/rectal haemorrhage - a high bleeding-risk overlap that needs immediate reconciliation.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13:50 and 19:36:45) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves and RR intervals ranging 346-720 ms - atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of about 134-136/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the note should be corrected and rate control/anticoagulation reviewed.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 7/12/2026-1/9/2027, started 11/10/2025). His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 72/min with QT 551 ms and RR 965 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of 561 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 6/9/2026), so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. He is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on continuous amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 6/17/2026-1/6/2027) plus metoprolol and warfarin. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 71/min with frequent atrial ectopy, QT 576 ms at RR ~1000 ms and a Bazett QTc of 576 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required, and a current ECG should be obtained as the only tracing on file is now more than four years old.

interpretations.explanation: 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm, mean ventricular rate 72/min (RR 788-924 ms, mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR 165 ms. Narrow QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT 356 ms at RR 838 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the 11/21/2025 tracing the rhythm is unchanged (sinus, though the earlier study had two atrial couplets with post-ectopic pauses) and the QTc has fallen markedly from 535 ms to 393 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

5/23/2024, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with a short-normal PR of 104 ms. QRS 86 ms, QS/rS in V1 without terminal R', no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +1 degree (normal). QT 317 ms at RR 615 ms, QTc 404 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

9/17/2024, the only ECG on file. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging 410-728 ms and no organised or reproducible atrial activity (median-beat P amplitude only about 0.07 mV with poor beat-to-beat correlation), so there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 109/min. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in I, giving a frontal axis of about -59 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 321 ms at RR 550 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. This is consistent with the charted diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin. No prior tracing for comparison.

1/13/2019. Sinus bradycardia, dominant RR 1112-1160 ms (about 53/min) with one late couplet (RR 584/586 ms); nine QRS complexes give a mean rate of 59/min. Upright P waves precede the sinus beats, PR 162 ms. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -11 degrees (normal). QT 392 ms at RR 1130 ms, QTc 369 ms. Compared with 12/13/2018 (sinus 66/min, PR 176 ms, QRS 104 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change; the new finding is the atrial/ventricular couplet.

4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm with frequent atrial ectopy: the dominant RR intervals are 970-1086 ms (sinus rate about 58/min) with four early beats (426-674 ms); 12 complexes in 10 s give a mean ventricular rate of 71/min. Low-amplitude but reproducible P waves (0.08-0.10 mV) are seen before the sinus beats on individual-beat review, with PR about 200 ms (borderline). QRS is narrow at 84 ms; frontal axis +43 degrees (normal). The T wave is very broad: QT 576 ms at RR about 1000 ms, Bazett QTc 576 ms - marked prolongation on amiodarone. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at 129/min with no P waves and QTc 449 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-900 ms) with upright P waves and PR 128 ms. QRS 98 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +33 degrees (normal). The T wave is late and broad: QT 504 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - significantly prolonged, relevant to his escitalopram therapy (the contemporaneous note called the QT 'acceptable'). Compared with 11/23/2022 (sinus 76/min, PR 120 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 367 ms) the QTc has increased by about 170 ms, a QTc increase of 60 ms or more; rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

8/23/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, metronomically regular (RR 716-726 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 140 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms with rS in V1 and a tall R in V6; no bundle branch block or AV block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 345 ms at RR 720 ms, QTc 407 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

7/13/2022. Sinus tachycardia at 141/min: RR intervals are regular at 404-454 ms and a reproducible P wave (peak about 0.09 mV in II/aVF, PR 120 ms) precedes each QRS. QRS 90 ms with a deep QS complex in V1; no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -9 degrees (normal). QT 278 ms at RR 426 ms, Bazett QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, chaotically irregular, no P waves) at 107/min with QTc 439 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

3/19/2025. Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular (RR 580-596 ms), tall upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 150 ms. QRS 92 ms; V1 shows an rSR' configuration with a small terminal S in I and V6, an incomplete right bundle branch block pattern that does not meet the 120 ms duration criterion, so no bundle branch block is reported. Frontal axis +45 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms at RR 590 ms, QTc 437 ms. Identical to the 3/18/2025 tracing (102/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 437 ms); no change.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are chaotically irregular from 346 to 720 ms, there is no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval, and mean ventricular rate is 136/min. QRS 98 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -2 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms at RR 416 ms, Bazett QTc 453 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (17:13) showed the same rhythm at 134/min with QTc 433 ms, so there is no change between studies. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, extremely regular (RR 494-502 ms). An upright P wave with PR about 190 ms precedes each QRS, followed by PR-segment depression. QRS 102 ms without a bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis +51 degrees (normal). QT 286 ms at RR 498 ms, QTc 405 ms. Compared with the 9/16/2016 tracing (sinus 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 403 ms) there is no significant change.

7/16/2022. Regular sinus rhythm at 91/min (RR 650-666 ms). Discrete upright P waves in II and aVF with PR 185 ms - within normal limits. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -44 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 342 ms at RR 658 ms, QTc 421 ms. Compared with the prior 5/16/2021 tracing the rhythm remains sinus, QRS duration is unchanged and QTc is similar (399 to 421 ms, <60 ms change); the axis has shifted leftward but no listed change category applies.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm, dominant RR 864-882 ms with one early beat; mean rate 72/min. The atrial deflection preceding each QRS is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (P axis roughly -80 degrees), which is not sinus - this is an ectopic low-atrial/left-atrial rhythm, hence classified as OTHER. PR 130 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; net frontal QRS axis about -26 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 413 ms at RR 875 ms, Bazett QTc 442 ms. The prior 4/27/2025 tracing showed the same inverted inferior P waves at 61/min with QTc 412 ms and a markedly different, extreme frontal axis (-174 degrees) suggesting limb-lead reversal on that study; no listed change category applies.

4/29/2026, the only ECG on file. Regular rhythm at 70/min (RR 842-884 ms) with a small consistent atrial deflection before each QRS and PR 134 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block. As recorded, the QRS is deeply negative in I and aVL and positive in III with a positive R in V6, giving a frontal axis of about -172 degrees, which falls in the extreme axis range; the discordance between the limb leads and the normal precordial progression, together with an inverted P wave in lead I, strongly suggests left-arm/right-arm electrode reversal, and this should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. QT 362 ms at RR 862 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal, which is reassuring given his escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation: RR intervals are grossly irregular (458-1150 ms), no discrete P waves are present (median-beat atrial amplitude about 0.02 mV, poor beat-to-beat correlation) and there is no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 70/min. QRS 96 ms with rS in V1, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +26 degrees (normal). QT 445 ms at RR 740 ms, Bazett QTc 517 ms - prolonged, in the context of amiodarone loading during this admission. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves (PR 170 ms) and QTc 403 ms, so this shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of more than 60 ms.

3/8/2026, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 856-906 ms), with tall upright P waves in II/aVF and PR 140 ms. QRS 96 ms, predominantly negative in V1 without a terminal R', so no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +54 degrees (normal). QT 430 ms at RR 880 ms, Bazett QTc 458 ms - upper normal/borderline but below the 500 ms review threshold, which is relevant as this tracing was obtained to screen his newly started escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

2/15/2025, the only ECG on file. Sinus rhythm at 76/min with only minor RR variation (mild sinus arrhythmia). Upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 185 ms - within normal limits. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis +55 degrees (normal). QT 384 ms at RR 810 ms, Bazett QTc 426 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus rhythm at 122/min, metronomically regular (RR 492-496 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 128 ms. QRS has narrowed to 96 ms and no longer meets criteria for bundle branch block. The QRS is predominantly negative in I, aVL and V6 and positive in III, giving a frontal axis of about +177 degrees - right axis deviation. QT 290 ms at RR 494 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (01:33), which showed a wide 164 ms QRS with a monophasic late-peaking R in V1 and broad S waves in I and V6 (right bundle branch block) and QTc 478 ms, the bundle branch block has resolved and the QTc has fallen by about 65 ms.

9/13/2025. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (312-604 ms), the baseline shows no organised atrial activity and there is no measurable PR interval; mean ventricular rate 147/min. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 84/min with discrete P waves (PR 140 ms) and frequent ectopy, QTc 425 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation; the QTc is unchanged.

3/7/2026, the only ECG on file.
